title: How does coax learn that a background shell command ended?
body:
coax's report to decade carries a `subagents` list (461c197). `Snapshot::of` in `report.rs` fills it from `Transcript::subagents`, which returns the top-level tool calls that start a sub-agent, the `Agent` or `Task` calls. A shell command the agent runs in the background is an ordinary tool call, and coax does not track it after the call completes. decade's `Subagent` is described as "a sub-agent or background task", so such a command belongs in the list too.

## Open

- What the Claude adapter v0.101.0 sends for a background shell command: whether its tool call stays in progress, completes at launch, or gets a later update when the command ends. The answer is in the adapter's bundled JavaScript or in a log of a live session.
- If nothing marks the end, whether coax can tell a background command is done at all.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/72a5a67e
notes.text:
Checked against the adapter's source, in a checkout of `claude-agent-acp` a little ahead of v0.101.0.

- A background Bash call goes `completed` at launch, with a result like "Command running in background with ID …". The adapter sends coax nothing more on that call.
- The adapter receives the SDK's `task_started`, `task_notification` and `background_tasks_changed` frames. It passes them on only to a client that declares the JetBrains AIR `asyncTasks` capability or the `terminal_output` meta. coax declares neither, in `src/acp.rs`.
- The adapter never holds a turn for a background shell. The comment on `liveBackgroundTasks` in `acp-agent.ts` says a hold must never wait on a shell.
- `_session/async_task/stop` takes `{sessionId, asyncTaskId}` and returns `{stopped}`. It works only for AIR clients. No method lists tasks.
- Not traced to the end: when the command exits, Claude Code probably wakes the model with a follow-up turn (`startAutonomousCycle`). coax would see that turn as agent text with no prompt open.

So coax cannot show a background command without declaring a new capability.

| path | what coax gets | cost |
|---|---|---|
| declare `terminal_output` | a terminal kept open on the call until the command ends, with its output and exit | coax handles terminal updates on every Bash call, foreground ones too |
| declare AIR `asyncTasks` | a full task lifecycle, and stopping | AIR changes other behaviour too, such as background sub-agents no longer holding the turn |
| read the launch result's text | the task's ID, and perhaps its end from the follow-up turn | no reliable end signal |

The lean is `terminal_output`, the one path with a real end signal that does not bring the rest of AIR. What declaring it changes for ordinary Bash calls is being read next.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/72a5a67e
notes.text:
What declaring `terminal_output` changes, read in the same adapter checkout.

- A client declares it with `"terminal_output": true` in `clientCapabilities._meta` (`ClientCapabilities.from` in `tool-calls/client-capabilities.ts`). The adapter does not read `terminal: true`. In coax this is one more key in the `_meta` map in `src/acp.rs`.
- Foreground Bash: the `tool_call` carries `_meta.terminal_info {terminal_id}`, and its `content` becomes `{"type": "terminal", "terminalId": ...}`. At the result the adapter sends one update with `_meta.terminal_output {terminal_id, data}` holding the whole output. A second update carries the status and `_meta.terminal_exit {terminal_id, exit_code, signal}`. The output no longer arrives as a text block in `content`, and `rawOutput` is left out. Nothing streams before the result.
- Background Bash: the call goes `completed` at launch, with the launch text in `terminal_output`. `withRunningTerminal` holds back `terminal_exit`. When the task ends, `endBackgroundTask` calls `taskEnded` in `background-work.ts`, which sends `terminal_exit` with `exit_code` null, killed or not. The status does not change. No output arrives while the command runs, since the live tail runs only for ACP v2 clients.
- If the session ends before the command, the adapter sends no `terminal_exit` to a v1 client.
- Reading the source found no effect on turn holds, sub-agents, queued prompts or permission requests.

Not confirmed: that the SDK's `task_notification` reaches `endBackgroundTask` for a client like coax, and that replay on `session/load` sends the terminal messages too. A live trial with a logged session would settle both.

Cost for coax: `Transcript` keeps no `_meta` beyond the parent link, and stores only `content`. Once coax declares the meta, Bash output moves out of `content`, so coax has to keep `terminal_output` and `terminal_exit` itself. Without that, Bash output would disappear from the transcript.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Checked a second way, against the JavaScript embedded in the adapter's bundled binary (v0.101.0 as installed) and the bundled Claude Code binary beside it. No live session was run. This agrees with the two earlier notes and adds the model's side.

## What the adapter sends for a background Bash call

- `backgroundBashTaskFromToolResult` recognises the tool result of a Bash call whose input has `run_in_background: true`. The result text starts "Command running in background with ID: ". The call is then reported `completed` at launch. It does not stay `in_progress`.
- The SDK later emits a `task_notification` frame with `task_id` and `status`. The adapter's `case "task_notification"` handler calls `endBackgroundTask`, which calls `taskEnded` on the session's background tracker.
- `taskEnded` acts only on a terminal or a tool call the tracker registered. `terminalStarted` registers a terminal only when the client declared `terminal_output` and is not an AIR client. Without that, `taskEnded` finds nothing and sends coax no message.
- `taskEnded` sends `terminalExit` for a registered terminal. For a registered tool call it sends a status update: completed, failed, or cancelled when the task was stopped. The tool-call registration belongs to the AIR path.
- `asyncTasks.taskNotification` forwards `task_started` and `task_notification` details only to an AIR client. `background_tasks_changed` is handled in the same loop and also drops tasks that vanish from the SDK's list.

So for coax as it declares capabilities today, the answer is: completed at launch, and no later `tool_call_update`.

## How the model learns the command ended

- The bundled Claude Code binary carries the tool text "You will be notified when it completes" next to "Command running in background with ID:". It also says the notice arrives "even after your final response, unless this session goes idle first". The model is told not to poll.
- The notice is a user-role message holding `<task-notification>` XML (fields `task-id`, `status`, `summary`, `output-file`, `tool-use-id`) inside a `<system-reminder>`. The adapter has `taskNotificationsOf` to parse exactly this tag from user messages.
- The adapter's main loop calls `startAutonomousCycle` for any top-level `assistant` or `stream_event` message that arrives with no foreground work open. That starts a turn the person did not prompt. So when the command ends while coax is idle, the model most likely gets woken, and coax sees agent output with no `session/prompt` pending. When a turn is open, the notice most likely lands in that turn.
- The output stays readable at the `output-file` path named in the launch result ("Output is being written to"). The model can read it with ordinary file tools. `BashOutput` appears in no string I found in the adapter, so I did not establish that it is part of this flow.

## Not established

- Whether the wake-up really happens in every case. The strings show the mechanism and the idle caveat, not a trace of a live run.
- Whether `task_notification` is sent for a background Bash call to a client like coax. The handler is not gated on capabilities, but the SDK side is in the Claude Code binary, which I only searched for strings.
- Exact meaning of "unless this session goes idle first". Possibly a long-idle session loses the notice.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/df584c97
notes.text:
Context, restated for the next session. coax reports an agent's running sub-agents to decade (`Snapshot::of` in `src/report.rs`), so decade's sidebar shows what the agent is busy with. A shell command the agent runs in the background is running work too, but coax cannot report it, because the adapter marks the call `completed` at launch and sends nothing when it ends (the research note above).

Agreed plan, not started:

1. Spike: find out what declaring `terminal_output` commits coax to in the Claude adapter v0.101.0, and whether the adapter then sends a `tool_call_update` when a background command ends. This needs only the adapter's code and the ACP schema, no login.
2. Decide: if it works, coax tracks background commands as running work and reports them to decade beside sub-agents. If the capability brings obligations coax cannot meet, decade shows sub-agents only and this issue closes.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4c7bb0a4
notes.text: The background commands milestone (coax-42022c) offers a fourth path that needs no capability. coax finds the shell behind each command in `/proc` (coax-97661c), and the command has ended when that PID is gone or its start time no longer matches. That signal works for a live session, and after coax restarts too. It reports no exit code, so `terminal_output` stays the path if coax ever needs the exit status.
